title: Annotatio IV §.XVIII: Wycliffe vs Transubstantiation — bread substance remains; naturally bread, sacramentally body
pass_a_gloss: Wycliffe thus contradicts TRANSUBSTANTIATION: The substance of bread remains on the altar after Consecration and does not cease to be bread. Likewise: The consecrated Host is naturally true bread, and sacramentally the body of Christ. Likewise: As Christ is at once God and man, so the consecrated host is at once the body of Christ and true bread: Because it is the Lord’s body IN FIGURE, and true bread IN NATURE.
pass_b_english: Wycliffe against Transubstantiation: after consecration the bread’s substance remains on the altar — it does not cease to be bread.
The consecrated Host is naturally true bread and sacramentally Christ’s body — at once body and true bread, as Christ is at once God and man: the Lord’s body IN FIGURE, true bread IN NATURE.
source_text: TRANSSUBSTANTIATIONI ita contradicit Wicleph: Substantia panis manet in altari post Consecrationem & non definit esse panis. Item: Hostia consecrata, est naturaliter verus panis, & sacramentaliter corpus Christi. Item: Sicut Christus est simul Deus & homo, ita hostia consecrata est simul corpus Christi & verus panis: Quia est corpus Domini IN FIGURA, & verus panis IN NATURA.
